pitch_detail.notes: Approach via Sunrise Mine Trail through brush to river crossing
Follow river valley and ascend main gully/slabs to 3,700 ft basin
Ascend steep gully or adjacent slabs toward southeast ridge
Traverse snow-covered slabs northwest to southeast ridge notch (5,600 ft)
Ascend south ridge via gully or exposed ridge crest to summit block
Final scramble to 6,020 ft summit
From Lake Constance into the upper canyon toward the North Chute's base.
Scree/snow couloir gaining the upper mountain from the north.
Joins the standard route's crux traverse below the summit block.
Final scramble and chimney to the true summit.
Lake Constance to base of South Chute.
Scree/snow chute to the South Ridge notch.
20-30 ft downsloping ledge, fingers jammed in the top crack; minimal footholds on the last few steps.
Snow basin, scree, and a final low-5th-class step to the true summit.
Bike-able logging roads to Dailey Prairie/Orsino Creek Basin
Talus and scree to a notch near ~5,200 ft below the ridge
Traverse south of the ridge crest via gullies and a seasonal snowfield, avoiding the Class 4 crux entirely
Final scramble to the true summit
Off-trail from Swamp Creek Trail, cross Swamp Creek (~3,600'), brush/timber to open basin (~4,000')
Scree/talus (possible lingering snow) up to a notch around 7,300'
Grassy ledges below a prominent white vertical rock band
Narrow, chossy gully through stacked boulders to the summit
Trail #96, ~4 mi and ~2,000 ft gain to camp.
Cross-country traverse of ribs and gullies at ~7,400-7,600 ft toward Gilbert Peak.
Solid, abrasive volcanic aggregate leads to the notch behind the black prow.
Short class 4 scramble through the notch to the true summit; loose in places.
